text: Vertically aligned anatase TiO2 nanotube arrays were anodized in fluoride electrolyte. Kubelka-Munk transformed diffuse reflectance data give an optical band gap of 3.23 eV for the pristine arrays and 2.85 eV after nitrogen doping.

Scanning tunneling spectroscopy on rutile TiO2(110) reveals a gap of 3.1 eV between the valence and conduction band edges. A hybrid-functional (HSE06) calculation of the same surface slab gives 3.4 eV.
Spectroscopic ellipsometry on SrTiO3 single crystals identifies an indirect optical gap at 3.25 eV and a direct optical gap at 3.75 eV at room temperature.

GaN high electron mobility transistors exploit the wide band gap of the material for high-voltage operation. Our device with a 25 nm AlGaN barrier shows a two-dimensional electron gas density of 1.0e13 cm-2, a breakdown voltage of 650 V and a threshold voltage of -3.2 V.

CdTe absorber layers were deposited by close-space sublimation at a substrate temperature of 400 °C. The absorption edge measured by UV-vis-NIR spectroscopy lies at 827 nm, which defines the band gap of the CdTe layer.

gold.evidence: absorption edge measured by UV-vis-NIR spectroscopy lies at 827 nm

text: Sputtered WO3 films were annealed at 300, 400 and 500 °C. The optical band gap derived from Tauc plots is 2.95 eV, 2.80 eV and 2.70 eV for the films annealed at 300, 400 and 500 °C, respectively.

Bulk graphitic carbon nitride (g-C3N4) prepared by thermal polycondensation of melamine has a band gap of 2.70 eV from UV-vis diffuse reflectance, whereas the exfoliated g-C3N4 nanosheets show a widened band gap of 2.88 eV.
For monolayer black phosphorus the PBE gap is 0.9 eV, whereas HSE06 raises it to 1.95 eV. FTIR absorption spectra of bulk black phosphorus crystals show an optical gap of 0.3 eV.
Hexagonal boron nitride films grown by CVD on Cu show a deep-UV absorption onset at 208 nm, corresponding to the band gap of the film. This agrees with the roughly 6 eV gap quoted in earlier reports.

AlN films were grown on sapphire by MOCVD. Transmission spectra at room temperature give an optical band gap of 6.03 eV for AlN, while Al0.5Ga0.5N alloy films prepared under the same conditions exhibit an optical band gap of 4.70 eV.

gold.evidence: optical band gap of 6.03 eV for AlN

text: AlxGa1-xN epilayers with different Al content were characterized by absorption spectroscopy. The band gap is 3.85 eV for x = 0.2 and 4.25 eV for x = 0.4, indicating a bowing parameter of about 1 eV.

DFT calculations with the PBE functional predict an indirect band gap of 1.31 eV for the double perovskite Cs2AgBiBr6. UV-vis absorption of our polycrystalline films, by contrast, shows an onset corresponding to a band gap of 2.19 eV.

From the first derivative of the external quantum efficiency spectrum, we determine the band gap of the FA0.85Cs0.15PbI3 absorber to be 1.56 eV. The cell has a short-circuit current density of 24.1 mA cm-2.

gold.evidence: band gap of the FA0.85Cs0.15PbI3 absorber to be 1.56 eV

text: The ideal top-cell gap for a perovskite/silicon tandem is 1.7-1.8 eV. We therefore tuned the halide composition and obtained CsPbI2Br films with a Tauc band gap of 1.91 eV, which is somewhat larger than the target.
ZnO nanorods were excited with a 325 nm He-Cd laser (photon energy 3.82 eV). The free-exciton binding energy is 60 meV and the optical band gap extracted from the absorption spectrum is 3.26 eV.

gold.evidence: optical band gap extracted from the absorption spectrum is 3.26 eV

text: Electrodeposited Cu2O shows a direct Tauc gap of 2.17 eV, whereas the CuO films obtained after thermal oxidation at 400 °C show a much smaller band gap of 1.35 eV.
The first absorption onset of colloidal CdSe quantum dots appears at 590 nm, and that of CdTe quantum dots at 760 nm; we define the optical band gap of each sample by this onset.

gold.evidence: CdSe quantum dots appears at 590 nm

text: Individual silicon nanowires with a diameter of 3 nm were probed by scanning tunneling spectroscopy, which reveals a band gap of 1.3 eV. Bulk silicon has a gap of 1.12 eV, so the nanowire gap is enlarged by quantum confinement.

gold.evidence: reveals a band gap of 1.3 eV

text: Single crystals of beta-Ga2O3 grown by the edge-defined film-fed method show an absorption edge at 255 nm. HSE06 calculations on the same structure give a band gap of 4.78 eV.

gold.evidence: give a band gap of 4.78 eV

text: MAPbI3 perovskite solar cells with a power conversion efficiency of 21.3% and an open-circuit voltage of 1.12 V were fabricated. Band gap engineering is expected to further improve the performance, but optical gap measurements are beyond the scope of this paper.
Measured band gaps of the SiC polytypes grown by physical vapor transport are 3.26 eV for 4H-SiC, 3.02 eV for 6H-SiC and 2.36 eV for 3C-SiC.
The HSE06 functional yields a band gap of 2.55 eV for scheelite-monoclinic BiVO4, slightly larger than the 2.45 eV measured on our photoanode by UV-vis spectroscopy.

gold.evidence: yields a band gap of 2.55 eV

text: Within DFT+U (Ueff = 4.3 eV on the Fe 3d states), hematite alpha-Fe2O3 has a calculated band gap of 2.0 eV with a spin-polarized antiferromagnetic ground state.
For wurtzite ZnO, LDA gives a band gap of only 0.75 eV, while the G0W0 quasiparticle gap is 3.4 eV, much closer to the measured 3.37 eV from the literature.

gold.evidence: LDA gives a band gap of only 0.75 eV

text: In dual-gated bilayer graphene, infrared spectroscopy shows that a perpendicular electric field of 2 V/nm opens a tunable band gap of 0.25 eV.
Photoluminescence of CVD-grown monolayer MoSe2 and WSe2 gives optical band gaps of 1.57 eV and 1.65 eV, respectively, at 300 K.
Hg0.78Cd0.22Te epilayers measured at 77 K have a long-wavelength cut-off of 10.2 µm, which corresponds to the narrow band gap of this alloy.
Oleate-capped PbS quantum dots with a 3.4 nm diameter show a first excitonic absorption peak at 1100 nm, which we use as the optical gap of the dots. The ligand exchange step was done at 25 °C.

gold.evidence: first excitonic absorption peak at 1100 nm

text: Tetragonal BaTiO3 thin films exhibit an optical band gap of 3.2 eV from Tauc analysis, while GGA-PBE calculations give a much smaller band gap of 1.7 eV.
Kesterite absorbers deposited by sputtering and sulfurization have optical band gaps of 1.5 eV for Cu2ZnSnS4 (CZTS) and 1.0 eV for Cu2ZnSnSe4 (CZTSe), as determined from absorption coefficient plots.
SnS thin films were thermally evaporated on glass at 250 °C and are p-type with a hole concentration of 1e17 cm-3. The band gap of the films was not determined in this work.
A random-forest model trained on DFT data predicts band gaps of 2.35 eV for Li3PS4 and 1.90 eV for Na3SbS4, with a cross-validated mean absolute error of 0.45 eV.

gold.evidence: band gaps of 2.35 eV for Li3PS4

text: MAPbBr3 single crystals show a band gap of 2.18 eV derived from the absorption spectrum. The photoluminescence peak is located at 2.28 eV and the Stokes shift is attributed to reabsorption.

gold.evidence: band gap of 2.18 eV derived from the absorption spectrum

text: A Varshni fit to temperature-dependent absorption data of silicon gives Eg(0) = 1.170 eV at 0 K with a coefficient alpha = 4.73e-4 eV/K.
The infrared absorption spectrum of ZnSe single crystals shows the absorption edge at 21800 cm-1, which is taken as the band gap energy.
Hydrogenated amorphous silicon films grown by PECVD have a Tauc gap of 1.75 eV and an E04 gap (energy at which the absorption coefficient reaches 1e4 cm-1) of 1.95 eV.
Scanning tunneling spectroscopy of MBE-grown Bi2Se3 films shows a bulk band gap of 0.3 eV, while the surface state forms a gapless Dirac cone inside this gap.
Tight-binding calculations for hydrogen-terminated silicon quantum dots yield band gaps of 2.9 eV for a diameter of 2 nm and 2.0 eV for 4 nm, demonstrating strong quantum confinement.

gold.evidence: 2.9 eV for a diameter of 2 nm

text: Regioregular P3HT films have an optical gap of 1.9 eV estimated from the absorption onset. Cyclic voltammetry gives a HOMO level of -5.0 eV and a LUMO level of -3.0 eV, i.e. an electrochemical gap of 2.0 eV.
The indirect band gap of GaP is 2.26 eV (548 nm) as measured by absorption spectroscopy at room temperature on polished wafers.

gold.evidence: indirect band gap of GaP is 2.26 eV
